title: SLA-aware backpressure + event-time deduplication for console metrics ingest
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Problem: Console ingest spikes from active customers (notably heavy dashboard refreshes and replay jobs) produce transient bursts that saturate downstream windowed aggregators. Current queueing is single-tenant-agnostic and drops older events during overload, leading to inaccurate per-tenant usage metrics and noisy billing deltas. We need an ingest pipeline that enforces per-tenant SLAs (latency and availability), applies graceful backpressure, and performs event-time deduplication to support late-arriving telemetry (network retries, browser reconnections).
goal: Introduce SLA-aware backpressure and an event-time deduplication layer at the front of the console metrics streaming pipeline so that: 1) high-traffic tenants cannot cause cross-tenant metric loss; 2) we maintain accurate time-windowed aggregates despite out-of-order or retried events; 3) graceful degradation prefers low-latency control plane metrics over non-critical telemetry during overload.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant ingest throttles configurable by SLA tier (free / standard / enterprise) and enforced at entry router
Pipeline preserves event-time ordering for windowed aggregations using watermarking that tolerates up to 45s of lateness
Exactly-once semantics for deduplicating retried events using a bounded state store (keyed by tenant+event_id) with TTL
Under a simulated 3x traffic spike, high-tier tenants maintain <=100ms p95 ingest latency while low-tier metrics may be delayed but not dropped silently
Automated dashboards surface throttling actions, queue depths, and dedupe hit/miss rates
End-to-end test harness and chaos scenario validated in staging (link to runs)
implementation_notes: Introduce an entry-layer router (Go) that consults tenant SLA metadata and assigns per-tenant tokens; tokens refill via leaky-bucket with burst allowance
Use Kafka topics partitioned by tenant-hash to keep per-tenant ordering; add a lightweight local in-memory admission queue per partition for short-term bursts
Implement deduplication as a streaming operator (Flink job) using RocksDB keyed state; store dedupe keys (tenant:event_id) with a 24-hour TTL, compacted via periodic cleanup
Adopt event-time watermarking with maxOutOfOrderness=45s to drive windowed aggregations; emit late-arrival metrics to a separate "late-events" topic for visibility
Expose backpressure signals to the router via a small HTTP/GRPC control plane that reports partition queue depth and consumer lag; router reduces acceptance rate if downstream lag > threshold
Fallback policy: if dedupe store unavailable, pipeline switches to best-effort de-dup by short-lived probabilistic bloom filter and records caveat in dashboards
Integration with Console: add per-tenant throttling audit logs and correlate throttling events with user sessions for SRE debugging
qa_plan: Unit tests for token bucket logic and per-tenant admission
Integration test: staged producer that replays events with out-of-order timestamps and retries; assert dedupe counts and final aggregates
Load test: 3x, 5x bursts with mixed tenant mix; assert p95 ingest latencies per tier
Chaos test: simulate RocksDB state loss and validate fallback bloom-filter mode and alerting
Staging Canaries: run for 72h on a cloned dataset before rollout

Control plane: expose queue depth / lag metrics and admission API (ENG-33324)
Dashboards: add throttling and dedupe KPIs to console-observability (ENG-33325)

notes: Trade-offs considered: strict exactly-once via global dedupe store was rejected because of cross-region latency; per-partition RocksDB provides acceptable guarantees with TTL and audit logs
We intentionally prioritize control-plane metrics (route decisions, SLA violations) for latency SLOs; non-critical diagnostic telemetry may be batched to reduce pressure
Operational considerations: need a maintenance job to prune stale dedupe keys and monitor RocksDB disk growth; include alerting on dedupe-store TTL exceedance
